squall.name: Squall
squall.message: Squall! The {ship} is taking a beating.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.message: Hurricane! The {ship} is fighting for her life.

calm.name: Becalmed
calm.message: The wind dies away. The {ship} lies becalmed, sails hanging limp.

norther.name: Norther
norther.message: A norther comes howling down from the Gulf. Cold wind, steep seas.

fog.name: Fog bank
fog.message: Fog closes in. The lookouts can barely see the bowsprit. Anything out there can't see you either.

_at_sea: Meetings at sea (scripts/at_sea.gd). rail_price: a merchant sells her cargo over the rail at this share of what it fetches where she's bound; plunder_price: a pirate sells hers at this share of the nearest port's price. gam_relation: standing with the Brethren a pirate needs to heave to and talk. tip_nm: how near a voyage's ports must be for a pirate to have heard of it. A friendly patrol asks to search you at inspect_chance (+ per point of notoriety); search_find: chance they find what you're hiding; clean_relation: thanks for a clean hold. npc_battle_days: how long other ships' fights last (time to come up and take a side). rescue_relation and rescue_gold_share: the thanks of a ship you saved.
_finds: Things floating at sea (events with a "find" key) put on the map for you to sail to: a daily chance of one appearing somewhere around you, how far off, how long it stays, and how close you must come. Storms leave wreckage in their wake; other ships' battles leave wreckage where they fought.

fish.spotted: birds diving on a shoal of fish

satchel.spotted: a canvas bag floating low in the water

_visibility: How far you see, and are seen, as a share of a clear day's sight: ships hidden by fog or dark can be slipped past, or crept up on.

quartermaster.name: Quartermaster
quartermaster.effect: Haggles in port: the better of captain's and quartermaster's Trade narrows the merchant's spread. Later: shares, discipline and votes.

navigator.name: Navigator
navigator.effect: Cuts the risk of running aground in shallows and adds a little speed.

boatswain.name: Boatswain
boatswain.effect: Drives the hands: reduces the speed penalty for sailing short-handed.

carpenter.name: Carpenter
carpenter.effect: Patches hull and sails at sea, up to 70% of full strength.

surgeon.name: Surgeon
surgeon.effect: Treats the wounded and sick (milestones 4 and 8).

skill_effects._comment: What each stat and skill does, shown in every stat tooltip (People.breakdown). Keep in step with the code that reads them.
skill_effects.authority: Battle: Hold steady, and standing up to their captain's threats and offers. Crew morale. The ransom asked if you're taken. A base manager's authority keeps it safe.
skill_effects.charisma: Battle: Rally the crew, Offer them quarter. Crew morale, recruiting in port, and how far a ringleader's word carries.
skill_effects.intimidation: Battle: Show them no mercy, Demand their surrender. Pressing contracts, and a base manager's grip on the town.
skill_effects.experience: Battle: who acts first each round.
skill_effects.seamanship: Captain: ship speed, 1% per point above or below 10. Boatswain: manoeuvres in battle (closing, the weather gauge, running) and working a short crew.
skill_effects.navigation: Navigator: fewer groundings in the shallows, and a little speed. With no navigator, the captain covers at half skill.
skill_effects.gunnery: Master gunner: broadsides in battle (with the crew's gunnery) and the guns in a siege. With no gunner, the captain covers at half skill.
skill_effects.swordplay: Captain: the duel with their captain when you board. Crew: their average swordplay carries boarding fights.
skill_effects.trade: Haggling in port: the better of the captain's and quartermaster's Trade narrows the merchant's spread. A base manager's Trade lifts its output.
skill_effects.carpentry: Carpenter: patching hull and sails at sea and in battle, remounting guns. A base manager's Carpentry speeds building. With no carpenter, the captain covers at half skill.
skill_effects.medicine: Surgeon: tending the wounded in battle, saving the badly hurt afterwards, and nursing the sick. With no surgeon, the captain covers at half skill.

fence._comment: Stolen goods: an honest port pays legal_mult of the price; a fence pays fence_mult, rising toward full price as you do business (trust_per_gold), but has only so much cash (refilling cash_regen of it a day). Silver and gold sold outside Spanish ports and fences fetch treasure_legal_mult.

bases._rebellion: Below rebel_below loyalty a base may rise (rebel_chance a day): the garrison (or a town's people) against the manager and your loyal men. A town's people number population / town_rebels_per; a cove's mutineers are half its garrison.
bases._shipbuilding: With a shipyard you can lay down a new hull. needs: further buildings for bigger ships. Cost is the ship's price times cost_mult; days are hull times days_per_hull (a good carpenter as manager is faster).

_sieges: Taking towns (scripts/sieges.gd, ui/siege_flow.gd). size: the fort (a modifier at full strength), the garrison, the walls (added to the defenders' roll), days of food behind the walls, and the gold a sack brings (x0.5 in a poor town, x1.5 in a rich one). A 'garrison' town has a stronger fort and more men; a pirate haven fewer. Capitals need a squadron of capital_min_ships. sides: where you land, and how much of the fort's fire falls there; one side, found by scouting, is weak. Holding a town makes it one of your bases (bases.max): it pays tax_base for its size plus tax_per_1000 people a day (times loyalty and the tax level; the buildings it came with cost nothing to keep up), and its old masters send an expedition (bases.raiders.expedition) every expedition_days.

sieges._memory: A siege you lift is remembered for memory_days: come back and the fort has repaired fort_repair_per_day points a day, the garrison has grown back garrison_regrow of the way a day, and the stores have filled up again.

hold._taxes: What you ask of a town you hold: mult on its taxes, loyalty added to what the town feels for you. loyal_defence: [loyalty, bonus]: a town at least that loyal helps defend itself. order and hunger: the town's mood (port life) moves loyalty by (order - 50) x order and hunger x hunger.
hold._expedition: Each beaten expedition makes the next one stronger (per_failure on its roll, men_per_failure more men); bigger towns draw bigger ones. lead_days before it's due, it sails from the nearest port of its nation, and you can catch it at sea.

crew._grudge: Hard times and good ones colour what each hand thinks of you (scripts/crew.gd mood_day). After after_days in a row with morale below `below`, every every_days each hand's opinion falls by 1 (by 1 more for the greedy while unpaid or idle of prey, and for drinkers while there's no rum), but hardship alone never takes it below `floor`: past that only your deeds can. After after_days above good_above it rises by 1 every every_days, up to good_cap. Battles (Crew.after_battle): struck the colours, lost more than heavy_losses of the crew, a prize taken (up to good_cap).

contracts._chains: grudge_trap: added to the trap chance of an employer you leaned on for full pay last time. kidnap_ransom: what a kidnapped grandee would fetch if you ransomed them yourself, times the reward. A blockade (each day you keep station within lurk_nm) cuts the port's imports and sailings to blockade_imports and adds blockade_hunger to the town's hunger.

ship_looks._comment: Paint, sails and figurehead: chosen at a shipyard (or your base's). Colours tint the ship's art. enemy_morale: off the enemy's morale when a fight starts; superstitious_morale/devout_morale: morale from crew with those traits (scaled by their share of the crew); no_false_colours: you can't pass as someone else.

black.name: Black
black.description: Every crew in the Caribbean knows what black sails mean: -5 to their morale when the fight starts. But nobody will believe your false colours.

mermaid.name: A mermaid
mermaid.description: The superstitious swear she keeps the ship lucky.

saint.name: A saint
saint.description: A comfort to the devout among the crew.

lion.name: A rampant lion
lion.description: Snarling gilt: -2 to the enemy's morale when the fight starts.

skull.name: A grinning skull
skull.description: -4 to the enemy's morale when the fight starts. Your own superstitious hands hate it.

adrift.name: Set them adrift in the boats
adrift.description: Merciful. Word of it will spread. Bloodthirsty hands will grumble.

maroon.name: Maroon them on a key
maroon.description: Harsh but not murder. Some will live.

kill.name: Put them to the sword
kill.description: Ruthless. Every captain in the Caribbean will hear of it. Some of your own crew won't forgive it.

balanced.name: Balanced
balanced.description: A fair share at sails, guns and the rail.

gun_deck.name: Gun deck
gun_deck.description: Every gun crewed and fast reloads. Clumsy handling, weak boarding.

boarders.name: Boarders
boarders.description: Muskets and cutlasses ready. Few guns manned.

runners.name: Runners
runners.description: Hands to the sails: best speed and turning in battle. Few guns, feeble boarding.

_endings: Endings you choose (scripts/endings.gd): retire with retire_gold to your name (purse and treasuries); become governor of a town you hold, with governor_standing with the nation that commissioned or pardoned you (and, for a privateer, at least rank governor_rank); found a republic at Nassau by leading its council and holding republic_towns towns. hang_chance: the chance a captain struck to the navy or hunters of a nation that wants them is hanged.
_diplomacy: Wars of the moment, between the dated ones in history.json (scripts/factions.gd). Each pair of nations has a tension, starting in start; it drifts each month by drift and rises with incidents (incident: a raid by one nation's privateer on the other's ships, a ship taken under the other's false colours, a sack). At war_at they go to war for war_months (at most max_wars at once); in a war tension falls by war_cools a month and each side may send an invasion squadron (invasion) against one of the other's smaller towns. Peace sets tension to peace_tension and hands each town back with return_on_peace.

diplomacy._invasion: capture_chance a month (per side at war) a squadron fits out against a smaller town of the enemy, due in days; it sails lead_days before, a ship of the type for the town's size, and on the day rolls strength (less the damage you did it) against the fort, walls and garrison/40. Beat it at sea and it's off: standing +rescue_relation with the town's nation.

career._bounty: The price on your head, by nation (Career.add_bounty): per_attack plus per_notoriety x the target's notoriety for each act of piracy, sack for sacking a town. It fades by decay_per_day. From hunt_from, hunters come: one more for every per_hunter gold, in the biggest ship whose threshold it passes. guarda_search: the chance a guarda costa stops a foreign ship with nothing to hide.

shipping._traders: Other ships besides the economy's merchants: smugglers running a Spanish port's contraband in from the Dutch and English islands, coasters carrying a port's own goods to a neighbour, and Spanish guarda costas.

dice_combat._conditions: What the light, the weather and the place do to a fight. Each battle has up to one of each, read from the world where it starts (scripts/combat/encounters.gd conditions()). gun: added to gunnery at each range band. actions: added to that action's roll for the side taking it. seamanship: to every manoeuvre. start_band: the ships sight each other late and start closer. gauge_flip: chance each round the wind shifts and the gauge changes hands. ends: chance each round it passes. becomes: after so many rounds it turns into another. surprise: morale the side attacked loses, caught unready. grounding: chance a deeper ship that fails a manoeuvre touches bottom. shallow_bonus: to the shallower ship's manoeuvres. sea_damage: hull both ships lose each round. fort: a port's guns join in.
dice_combat._temperaments: How an enemy captain fights, from their traits (the first that matches): it changes the AI's orders and her crew's starting morale. Shown in the battle log, and in a sighting when you know the captain by name.

bold.name: bold
bold.text: they'll come straight at you and won't run until the ship is sinking under them

timid.name: timid
timid.text: they'll keep their distance, and break off the moment it goes badly

greedy.name: greedy
greedy.text: they want your ship whole: expect chain and grape, and a demand to strike

steady.name: steady
steady.text: an old hand: they'll look for your weak points and hammer them

dawn.name: First light
dawn.text: Grey dawn: the lookouts are only now rubbing their eyes. The attacker has the gauge and the other side's crew are caught half awake.

dusk.name: Dusk
dusk.text: The sun is going down. Hold out until dark and the night will hide whoever wants to run.

night.name: Night
night.text: Only the gun flashes show where she is. Long shots are wasted; a ship that runs may vanish into the dark.

fog.name: Fog
fog.text: A wall of white. You sighted each other late and close. At range you're firing at a shadow, and a quick ship can lose herself in it.
fog.end_text: The fog thins and lifts: now everyone can see everyone.

squall.name: Squall
squall.text: Rain in sheets and the wind boxing the compass. The gauge won't stay with anyone for long.
squall.end_text: The squall blows through and the sun comes out.

norther.name: Norther
norther.text: A cold gale out of the north and steep seas. Gun ports ship water on the lee side.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.text: Madness: fighting in a hurricane. The sea is the worst enemy here, and it hits both ships.

calm.name: Dead calm
calm.text: Not a breath of wind. Neither ship can manoeuvre much: whoever has the better guns wins. A steady deck makes for good shooting.
calm.end_text: A breeze ruffles the water: the ships can move again.

shoals.name: Shoal water
shoals.text: Reefs and sandbars all round. A shallow keel goes where a deep one dares not, and a deep ship that blunders may touch bottom.

fort.name: Under the guns of {port}
fort.text: The fort at {port} is close enough to join in.

crits.text: A powder flash tears through a gun crew!

dice_combat._threat_wear: Each threat (Show them no mercy, Offer them quarter) after the first in a fight is this much harder: they've heard it before. One that fails heartens them by threat_backfire morale.
dice_combat._cripple: A ship with her sails below this fraction, or a mast gone, is crippled: her crew lose heart once, she's easier to hit, can't bring her own guns to bear, and is easier to talk into striking.

tips.steel: Steel: a duel, or winning the melee
tips.helm: Outsailing her: closing, the gauge, grappling
